source.title: Bigger Isn't Always Memorizing: Early Stopping Overparameterized Diffusion Models
source.authors: Alessandro Favero; Antonio Sclocchi; M. Wyart

record.tranche_reason: It measures validation or test loss over training time in diffusion models and a toy neural network, but does not reproduce the original double-descent size-sweep method.
record.gate_note: The study reports loss trajectories and memorization timing as training proceeds. It does not measure test error across model sizes or test error as a function of sample size near an interpolation threshold. Cited results from other work are not included as rows. Copy rates, image similarity, generated-data validity, and FID are not rows for the claim versions because they are not test-error measures.
record.test_reason: The study tracks held-out (validation or test) loss over training time in heavily overparameterized diffusion models and a toy score-fitting network. That is a new setting for epoch-wise curves (V2). The loss falls, then rises at memorization onset, and no second descent is reported through the end of training. It does not sweep model size or test whether more samples raise test error.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that diffusion-model learning is a competition of time scales: generalization improves first, then memorization begins at τmem ∝ P. They recommend early stopping that scales with dataset size, and they explicitly contrast this with noisy-regression double descent and benign overfitting.
record.recipe_differences: The study tracks training-time loss, copying, and memorization in diffusion models and a toy score-learning network; it does not reproduce the original supervised-learning model-size or sample-size double-descent sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: Memorization onset time changes with dataset size and diffusion noise level; the study reports that onset time is insensitive to batch size in the toy-network experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Memorization onset time grows roughly linearly with training-set size across image, text and grammar diffusion models. Kernel theory gives τmem ∝ P/σ^ν.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In overparameterized diffusion models, the training time at which held-out loss starts rising (memorization onset) scales proportionally with dataset size.

record.problems: For the loss trajectories relevant to V2, numerical values and uncertainty estimates are not stated in the text; the curves are presented as figures. The experiments concern diffusion objectives and score fitting rather than standard supervised test-error settings.
record.rows_left_out: Excluded generated-copy fractions, image similarities, FID, and grammar-validity results because they are not test-error measures for these versions. Also excluded the CelebA output-similarity trajectory for the same reason.

untested.parts: No model-size sweep of test error.
Training-set size is varied, but test error versus sample size near an interpolation threshold is not examined. Larger P only delays memorization.
No capacity sweep across model classes.
No effective-complexity measure predicting peak location.
No label-noise or regularization manipulation, and no multiple peaks.
No reparameterization of the complexity axis.
Standard supervised classification with label noise (the original setting) is not tested.

missing.what: FID over training for iDDPM on 16,384 CIFAR-10 images: decreases monotonically until τmem, then gradually increases. This is a generation-quality curve over training with no second descent.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not framed as a double-descent test. The authors argue diffusion memorization differs from supervised overfitting, where overparameterization can help. The V2 bearing rests on figure-only loss curves showing fall-then-rise without a later fall. Because no numbers are given and the claimed absence is not stated explicitly, limits_scope is used rather than challenges. Validation loss here is a diffusion variational bound, not classification error.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep of model size measuring test error around an interpolation threshold.
The study measures loss during training, but does not report a complete fall-rise-fall test-error curve or test this pattern in standard supervised tasks.
Dataset size is varied, but the study does not test whether increasing sample size raises test error near an interpolation threshold.
No general double-descent curve is tested across model classes.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested as predicting peak locations across axes.
The study does not test label-noise or regularization dependence, multiple peaks, or disappearance of a peak under optimal regularization.
The study does not compare parameter-count and effective-complexity measurements of a double-descent curve.
